claims.text: ALD at 150–250 °C can produce a conformal CeO2 overlayer below 2–3 nm on the nearly equiatomic multi-element automotive catalyst.
The deposited CeO2 will form a precisely controlled nanoscale shell on the underlying catalyst.
The CeO2 shell will have high oxygen-storage capacity.
The ALD treatment will create engineered oxygen vacancies at the CeO2–catalyst interface.
The CeO2 overlayer will act as a protective, self-regenerating barrier.
The CeO2 overlayer will minimize sintering of the underlying catalyst during transient operation and thermal stress.
The CeO2 overlayer will minimize elemental leaching from the underlying catalyst.
The CeO2 overlayer will reduce poisoning of the catalyst.
Interfacial oxygen vacancies will facilitate redox cycling.
Interfacial oxygen vacancies will facilitate activation of NO.
Interfacial oxygen vacancies will facilitate activation of water-derived species.
The proposed barrier and redox functions will preserve the accessibility and activity of underlying PGM sites during transient operation and thermal stress.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the ALD-modified catalyst will have lower light-off temperatures under low-temperature transient exhaust conditions.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the ALD-modified catalyst will have higher low-temperature conversion efficiencies.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the ALD-modified catalyst will deactivate more slowly during transient operation and accelerated thermal aging.
The CeO2 treatment will retain low platinum-group-metal consumption.
The predicted improvements apply within approximately 150–300 °C in transient exhaust containing H2O and NO.
An excessively thick CeO2 overlayer could impede reactant access to active sites.
